title: Settling In
content:
Chocolate arrived home three days ago and has been busy exploring every corner of her new cage. She spent the first night rearranging all of the bedding into one enormous pile in the back-left corner, then tunnelled through it for several hours. The wheel sensors recorded her first tentative spins just after midnight — only a few metres, but she seemed very pleased with herself.

She has discovered the scatter-feeding tray and appears to be hoarding sunflower seeds somewhere underneath the bedding mound. We have not found the stash yet, but the suspicious bulge suggests it is substantial.

title: First Marathon Night
content:
Last night the data logger recorded Chocolate's longest single run so far: 2.3 km on wheel 1 between 01:14 and 03:47. That is a personal best by a comfortable margin. The average speed over the session was 0.31 m/s, with a peak of 0.89 m/s just after 02:30 — she must have been in a real hurry.

By dawn she had also clocked 45 minutes on the ground floor and 20 minutes on the middle level, suggesting a full night of activity. The motion sensors on the top level were quiet, which usually means she was saving energy for the wheel.

title: Vet Check — All Clear
content:
Chocolate had her first veterinary check-up today. The vet confirmed she is in excellent health: a healthy weight of 42 g (right in the middle of the normal range for a Russian Dwarf), bright eyes, clean teeth, and a glossy coat.

The vet was impressed to hear about the monitoring system and joked that Chocolate probably has better fitness tracking than most humans. We are pleased to report that all those kilometres on the wheel are doing her good. Next check-up is scheduled for spring.

title: Winter Habits
content:
As the days have grown shorter, Chocolate's activity patterns have shifted noticeably. She now starts her main running session about an hour later than she did in autumn — typically beginning around 22:00 rather than 21:00 — and her longest active periods tend to cluster between midnight and 04:00.

She also seems to spend more time on the middle and top levels of the cage during daytime naps, perhaps because the heat rises and those platforms are a little warmer. Total daily distances are slightly down compared to October, but still averaging a respectable 1.4 km per night across both wheels.
